name: Barrie–Newmarket / Barrie corridor
description: Local and connecting bus services through Barrie, Stroud, Churchill, Bradford, Holland Landing, East Gwillimbury, Newmarket and Aurora. Express and rail-connection variants differ substantially by year.

timeline.event: The original timetable shows Barrie Bus Terminal–Barrie South–Bradford–Holland Landing–Newmarket, including a Bradford short service.
Allandale Waterfront appears in the route 68 timetable and corridor diagram.
Barrie train expansion was accompanied by reworked connecting buses, including Aurora connections.
The timetable documents the Barrie–Aurora corridor through East Gwillimbury and Newmarket GO.
Branches serving Barrie and its rail connection points remain in the original Barrie schedule.

sources.title: GO Barrie Table 65, printed June 27, 2009; archive filename October 7
GO revises routes and services, December 30, 2017 / January 2018 — Transit Toronto

gaps: The historical road names Highway 11 and Yonge Street refer to the same older north–south corridor in several timetable labels.
Branch suffixes have changed and been reused. Do not apply present-day 68A/68B meanings to the 2009 table.
These are documented dated snapshots. Changes between snapshots, temporary diversions and every historical local stop have not all been recovered.

GTFS dates identify captured feeds, not necessarily the first or last day of a route. Open a pattern to see its exact scheduled service dates. Temporary rail replacement and special-service patterns are included when present in the source.
Manually reconstructed versions generally contain published timetable timing points / major stops. They must not be read as complete roadside stop inventories.
